title: Probabilistic trace-linking shim and jitter-aware span sampling for streaming SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, opt-in SDK shim and edge proxy companion that probabilistically links request fragments when standard trace headers are missing or mutated, and implement a jitter-aware span sampler to avoid correlated sample loss for streaming and long-lived connections. Goal: improve trace continuity for debugging and SLO analysis while keeping CPU/memory overhead <1% and payload increase minimal.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with SDK, runtime, and telemetry teams. Agreed on opt-in default, deterministic seed derived from per-request fingerprint, and conservative link confidence scoring.
2026-02-20: Prototype Node SDK shim implemented (branch: feat/trace-link-shim). Microbenchmarks show ~0.12ms median overhead on simple request path. Early results reviewed with observability PM.

2026-02-28: Raised privacy and compliance concerns from Security — must ensure no PII is used for fingerprinting and include explicit opt-out and data retention controls. Created security review ticket.

2026-03-03: Design review with Edge/Proxy team. Decided to use a compact 2-byte probabilistic tag appended to existing instrumentation header when available; proxy will forward unchanged if not recognized. Fallback: additive X-Redwood-Trace-Approx header with confidence float (0.0-1.0) encoded as integer 0-255.

2026-03-07: Integration tests added to CI for Node and Python SDKs. Found race where streaming SDKs emitted spans before fingerprint stabilized — introduced a 1ms debounce to stabilize linkage without impacting latency by >0.2ms.

2026-03-10: Canaries configured in staging. Observability dashboards updated to surface linked-trace ratio and false-link rate metric. Plan to run a 2-week canary with gradual ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% of traffic.
Next steps: finish Go SDK implementation, complete Security review, and prepare rollout runbook and rollback thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: SDK shim available in Node, Python, and Go; published packages with semver bump and opt-in flag
Edge proxy recognizes and forwards probabilistic tags without breaking existing headers
E2E tests show less than 2% increase in 50th percentile latency for traced requests with shim enabled
False-link rate (as measured by synthetic trace ground-truth job) < 1% at default confidence threshold
Security review completed and Confluence doc updated with privacy model and retention controls
Dashboards show linked-trace ratio, sample-entropy, and alert when false-link rate > 1% or latency delta > 5%
